gap: No result ChatGPT got states how a Birdfy feeder's free AI ID and solar charging held up in a named reviewer's count: MacRumors' Juli Clover counted 47 visits in which the app correctly identified 38 birds, marked 14 unknown and got 2 wrong (about 70% right). Over five months on solar, her feeder in morning and afternoon sun never dropped below 90% charge, while one in a wooded spot hovered around 50%.
standout_why: Reviewed.com (cited, updated 2026-11-06) gives no battery percentage and no ID tally for any Birdfy or Birdbuddy model. It says only that the Metal 2 4K 'stayed consistently charged', and its single counted figure is 78 notifications for a Harymor feeder. Feeder Field (2026-10-30) says it was 'researched, not hands-on tested' and measured neither ID accuracy nor battery days. Birdfeederlab's Bird Buddy vs Birdfy page (2026-08-15) has only maker claims. Digital Camera World's roundup (2026-10-09) and its Kiwibit 2 Pro review have no battery or ID numbers. I could not open either WIRED page (the cited Nook vs Rookie piece or the best-of list): WebFetch is blocked there and curl needed approval I didn't get. So I can't rule out that WIRED has comparable counts, and I scored 2 rather than 3.
decides: It backs up the 'Birdfy for free AI ID' pick with a real count, and adds a caveat: in one reviewer's log, roughly 1 bird in 4 came back 'unknown' (14 of 54 birds) and 12 of 73 visits on another day went unidentified. It also shows that where the panel goes matters more than battery size: full sun kept the feeder at 90% or more with no manual charging, and a wooded spot meant about 50% and one winter recharge. It does not decide Birdfy vs Birdbuddy, because I found no comparable named count for any Birdbuddy model.
